title: Summary Of The Question And Answer The Risale I Nurs Duty Of Universal Repair

questions.question: What main question starts the imaginary discussion?
questions.answer: It asks why so much more effort is still being made for faith and tawhid when even a small part of the work is already very powerful.

questions.question: According to the passage, how strong is even a tiny portion of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It is described as strong enough to defeat the arguments of even a very stubborn denier.

questions.question: What comparison is used to show that the problem is very large, not small?
questions.answer: The work is compared to repairing a huge fortress of Islam, not fixing a little bit of damage or a small house.

questions.question: What does the passage say the fortress contains?
questions.answer: It contains Islam.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the size of the stones in that fortress?
questions.answer: They are pictured as being as large as mountains.

questions.question: Besides helping one person’s inner life, what larger things is the Risale-i Nur trying to heal?
questions.answer: It is trying to heal the shared heart, common ways of thinking, and public conscience of people.

questions.question: What has caused these deep problems in society, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Corrupting forces built up over a very long time have damaged them in a serious way.

questions.question: What has happened to the foundations and signs of Islam?
questions.answer: They are being torn down, and because of that the public conscience is being harmed.

questions.question: Why are these Islamic foundations and signs especially important for many believers?
questions.answer: They are a shelter and support for everyone, especially for ordinary believers.

questions.question: What kind of proofs are needed for such huge spiritual damage?
questions.answer: Proofs that are extremely certain and very strong are needed.

questions.question: What kind of treatment is needed for these wounds?
questions.answer: Powerful spiritual cures and many effective remedies are needed.

questions.question: From where does the passage say the Risale-i Nur gets its power to do this work?
questions.answer: It comes from the miraculous guidance of the Qur’an.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one more role of the Risale-i Nur besides repairing damage?
questions.answer: It also helps people move forward through endless levels of faith.

questions.question: What feeling does the speaker show after listening to the discussion?
questions.answer: He feels deep gratitude to Allah.

questions.question: Why might someone be surprised by the intense effort being put into the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because even a very small amount of it already seems enough to answer strong unbelief.

questions.question: What does the answer say the Risale-i Nur is not limited to doing?
questions.answer: It is not only fixing a small personal problem or helping just one person’s heart.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the scale of the destruction?
questions.answer: The damage is shown as something done to a huge stronghold connected to Islam.

questions.question: What does this image help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that the crisis is widespread and serious.

questions.question: Which three large areas of human life are said to need healing?
questions.answer: The shared heart, common thought, and general conscience.

questions.question: What tools are said to have made these breaches?
questions.answer: Instruments of corruption prepared over many centuries.

questions.question: What does the long time period mentioned in the passage suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the harm is deep-rooted and did not appear all at once.

questions.question: What are the medicines used for healing, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are the truths of the Qur’an, belief, and the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: Why are ordinary, weak proofs not enough in this situation?
questions.answer: Because the wounds are huge, so only very certain and powerful proofs can answer them.

questions.question: How does the passage emphasize the strength needed in those proofs?
questions.answer: It compares their strength to mountains.

questions.question: How does the passage emphasize the effectiveness needed in the remedies?
questions.answer: It says they should be as effective as a great many cures combined.

questions.question: What source does the Risale-i Nur come from in this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as coming forth from the Qur’an’s miraculous power.

questions.question: What two big jobs of the Risale-i Nur are mentioned?
questions.answer: It repairs major spiritual damage and helps believers rise in faith.

questions.question: What can we infer about the goal of this work from the whole passage?
questions.answer: Its goal is to protect and strengthen faith on both the personal and community level.

questions.question: In the opening of the passage, what kind of conversation is being described?
questions.answer: An imagined question-and-answer discussion.

questions.question: What concern does the questioner raise about the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: The questioner wonders why the work keeps expanding its efforts so strongly.

questions.question: What reason does the questioner give for asking that?
questions.answer: Because even a tiny portion is said to be enough to answer very stubborn disbelief.

questions.question: How does the response show that the mission is much bigger than it may first seem?
questions.answer: It says the work is dealing with massive destruction affecting Islam as a whole.

questions.question: What is the difference between repairing a small house and repairing the fortress in the passage?
questions.answer: A small house stands for limited personal damage, while the fortress stands for a huge, shared religious structure.

questions.question: What does the passage say is being treated besides an individual conscience?
questions.answer: Wider patterns of belief and the moral awareness of society are also being treated.

questions.question: What do the breaches in common thought and conscience show about the problem?
questions.answer: They show that the problem has spread beyond individuals into the wider community.

questions.question: According to the passage, how were these corrupting influences prepared?
questions.answer: They were built up and stored over about a thousand years.

questions.question: What does the word picture of “wounds” suggest about the condition being described?
questions.answer: It suggests painful, serious harm that needs healing, not just simple correction.

questions.question: Why are very powerful spiritual medicines necessary?
questions.answer: Because the injuries are broad and severe.

questions.question: What gives the Risale-i Nur the ability to carry out this task?
questions.answer: Its connection to the miraculous message of the Qur’an gives it that ability.

questions.question: Is the work only defensive in this passage, or is it also growth-oriented? Explain.
questions.answer: It is both, because it heals damage and also helps believers advance to higher levels of faith.

questions.question: What response does the listener have to the discussion?
questions.answer: He responds with great thankfulness.

questions.question: What is the central topic of this passage?
questions.answer: The purpose of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What challenge is raised about that purpose?
questions.answer: The challenge asks why more preparation is needed when the work already seems highly effective.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Risale-i Nur is working for?
questions.answer: It is working for faith and for proving Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the answer suggest about the size of the spiritual crisis?
questions.answer: It suggests the crisis is enormous and affects the Muslim community in a broad way.

questions.question: What picture is used to represent Islam in danger?
questions.answer: Islam is pictured as a giant fortress under damage.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention stones like mountains?
questions.answer: To show the greatness, weight, and seriousness of what is being protected and repaired.

questions.question: What personal areas are mentioned before the passage moves to society as a whole?
questions.answer: A private heart and an individual conscience.

questions.question: What social areas are mentioned after that?
questions.answer: The common heart, accepted ideas, and public conscience.

questions.question: What has attacked those social areas?
questions.answer: Corrupting forces and influences have attacked them.

questions.question: For whom are those Islamic supports especially important?
questions.answer: They are especially important for the larger body of believers.

questions.question: What kind of certainty must the needed proofs have?
questions.answer: They must have the highest level of certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Risale-i Nur is doing in this time?
questions.answer: It is carrying out this healing and strengthening mission in the present age.

questions.question: What can a student conclude about why the work is so detailed and forceful?
questions.answer: It is detailed and forceful because the harm it addresses is deep, widespread, and dangerous.

questions.question: Who speaks first in the imagined exchange, and what does that person ask about?
questions.answer: A questioner speaks first and asks why such intense effort continues in the work for belief.

questions.question: What has been increasing, according to that questioner?
questions.answer: The large-scale preparation and readiness of the Risale-i Nur have been increasing.

questions.question: What does the questioner believe a small portion of the work can already do?
questions.answer: It can overcome the objections of someone very stubborn in disbelief.

questions.question: How does the reply correct a narrow view of the work?
questions.answer: It explains that the mission is not small or private but vast and communal.

questions.question: What is one image in the passage that shows the mission is communal?
questions.answer: The image of rebuilding a huge fortress shows that the work concerns the whole community.

questions.question: What is one statement in the passage that shows the mission is not only personal?
questions.answer: It says the work is not just about fixing one person’s heart or conscience.

questions.question: What means are used for healing in the passage?
questions.answer: The healing comes through the Qur’an, faith, and the Qur’an’s miraculous truth.

questions.question: What had been prepared over many years to harm people?
questions.answer: Methods and tools of corruption had been prepared over a long period.

questions.question: How is the damage to shared beliefs described?
questions.answer: It is described as severe breaches and deep wounds.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress strong evidence so much?
questions.answer: Because weak answers would not be enough for such major attacks on faith.

questions.question: What does the phrase about endless levels of faith teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that faith can keep growing stronger and deeper.

questions.question: So is the Risale-i Nur only for bringing people back from doubt?
questions.answer: No, it is also for helping believers continue to rise spiritually.

questions.question: What kind of method does the speaker use to explain the purpose of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: He uses a summarized imagined dialogue.

questions.question: What two subjects is the Risale-i Nur said to be especially prepared to serve?
questions.answer: Belief and the proof of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What makes the questioner wonder whether more effort is necessary?
questions.answer: The questioner sees that even a very small amount of the work is already extremely convincing.

questions.question: How does the answer describe the damage being faced?
questions.answer: It describes it as large, widespread, and deeply harmful.

questions.question: What does the image of a citadel teach about Islam in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that Islam is something strong and precious that protects people, yet it has been heavily attacked.

questions.question: What shows that the attack is aimed at community life, not just individuals?
questions.answer: The passage talks about harm to shared thinking and the conscience of society.

questions.question: What are some things whose destruction is causing corruption in conscience?
questions.answer: The underlying supports, movements, and visible signs of Islam are being destroyed.

questions.question: Why is this especially dangerous for the masses of believers?
questions.answer: Because many believers depend on those supports as a refuge and guide.

questions.question: What kind of “equipment” is needed to answer this crisis?
questions.answer: Very certain, powerful, and solid evidence is needed.

questions.question: What kind of “medicine” is needed to answer this crisis?
questions.answer: Strong and highly effective spiritual remedies are needed.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does the Risale-i Nur emerge from?
questions.answer: It emerges from the miraculous nature of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What work does it perform after emerging from that source?
questions.answer: It serves as a cure for great spiritual damage and strengthens faith.

questions.question: What future-facing role does it also have?
questions.answer: It helps believers move ahead through unlimited stages of iman.

questions.question: What overall answer is given to the opening question?
questions.answer: More effort is needed because the sickness is huge, the harm is old and widespread, and only a powerful Qur’anic response can properly heal it.
